<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par118 />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=13}}, &c.); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=2}}, 19,<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=דֶּ֫רֶךְ}} is not to be taken as an ''accus. loci'' (''on the way''), but as an ''accus. of respect (with regard to the way)''; see below, m.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=7|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=9|verse=14|hidebook=1}}. On {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=30}} see {{GHGpar|116|i}}; on {{GHGheb|text=יָּשַׁב}}, with the ''accus. loci'', see {{GHGpar|117|bb}}. On the other hand, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=6|verse=3}}, according to the LXX, a verb of ''giving'' has dropped out before {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫רֶץ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|h}}
Examples of (''c''): {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=20}} ''fifteen cubits upward did the waters prevail''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=40|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=רַק הַכִּסֵּא אֶגְדַּל מִמֶּ֫ךָּ|translate=only in the throne will I be greater than thou}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=19}} ''we went'' (through) ''all that great and terrible wilderness''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=3}}. Of the same kind also are such cases as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=16}} (''according to the number of your persons'', for which elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=לְמִסְפַּר־}} is used); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=4}} (with the accus. preceding); 6:18, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=21|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=5}}.—A statement of weight is put in the accusative in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=26}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|i}}
'''3.''' The accusative is employed to determine more precisely the ''time'' (''accus. temporis''), (''a'') in answer to the question ''when?'' e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַיּוֹם|translate=the day}}, i.e. ''on the day'' (in question), ''at that time'', but also ''on this day'', i.e. ''to-day'', or finally ''by day'', equivalent to {{GHGheb|text=יוֹמָם}}, like {{GHGheb|text=עֶ֫רֶב|translate=at evening}}, {{GHGheb|text=לַ֫יְלָה|translate=noctu}}, {{GHGheb|text=בֹּ֫קֶר|translate=in the morning, early}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=4}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=צָֽהֳרַ֫יִם|translate=at noonday}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=91|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם אֶחָד|translate=on one and the same day}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=45}}; {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁנָא|translate=in sleep}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=127|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=תְּחִלַּת קְצִיר שְׂעֹרִים}} ({{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּתְ׳}}) ''at the beginning of barley harvest'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=21|verse=9}}; in stating a date, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=4|hidebook=1}} ''in the thirteenth year''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|k}}
(''b'') In answer to the question ''how long?'' e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=14}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־יְמֵי חַיֶּ֫יךָ|translate=all the days of thy life}}; 7:4 ''forty days and forty nights''; 7:24, 14:4, 15:13, 21:34, 29:18, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=9}} (''for six days''); 23:15, 31:17; {{GHGheb|text=עֽוֹלָמִים|translate=for ever}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=13}}; also with the accusative made determinate, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=13|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵת שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים|translate=throughout the seven days}} in question, mentioned immediately before; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=9|verse=25}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|l}}
'''4.''' The accusative is sometimes used of abstract ideas to state the reason (''accus. causae''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=25}} ''thou shalt not come thither'' {{GHGheb|text=יִרְאַת שָׁמִיר|translate=for fear of briers}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|m}}
'''5.''' Finally the accusative is used very variously (as an ''accus. adverbialis'' in the narrower sense), in order to describe more precisely the ''manner'' in which an action or state takes place. In English such accusatives are mostly rendered by ''in, with, as, in the form'' or ''manner of ..., according to, in relation to, with regard to''. For more convenient classification we may distinguish them as—

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|n}}
(''a'') Adjectives expressing ''state'', placed ''after'' the verb to describe more accurately some bodily or other external condition, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=20|verse=2}} ''walking'' {{GHGheb|text=עָרוֹם וְיָחֵף|translate=naked and barefoot}}; cf. verse 3, 8:21, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=18|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=שָׁלֵם}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=107|verse=5}} (but in 15:2 {{GHGheb|text=תָּמִים}} is rather a substantive directly dependent on {{GHGheb|text=הוֹלֵךְ}} = ''he that walketh'' in ''uprightness''; cf. {{GHGpar|117|r}}, note); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=28}}. After an accusative, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=18}}; to specify some mental state, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=35}} ({{GHGheb|text=אָבֵל}}).—''Before'' the verb (and then with a certain emphasis), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=2|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=5|verse=14}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=20|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=26|hidebook=1}}<section end=par118 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
